sections.h2: Who bills and values property in Putnam County?
sections.html:
Putnam County's property appraiser sets the value and decides exemptions, and the Putnam Tax Collector bills, collects and distributes the money. Changes to name, address or assessed value on the roll go through the appraiser, not the collector.

The appraiser's main office is at 312 Oak Street in Palatka, with a mailing box at PO Box 1920, Palatka, FL 32178. Crescent City and Interlachen have satellite offices that open on set days: Crescent City on Mondays and Wednesdays, Interlachen on Tuesdays and Thursdays. The exemption department's number is (386) 329-0286. The Tax Collector keeps its property tax pages at putnamtax.com and runs tax certificate sales through an online bidding site.

  • Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, tangible personal property, roll corrections.
  • Tax Collector: bills, discounts, installments, delinquent taxes and certificates.
  • Clerk of the Court: tax deed sales and recorded deeds.

sections.h2: Which taxing authorities appear on a Putnam County bill?
sections.html:
A Putnam bill can carry lines from the county, a fire district, the school board, two water management districts and one of five municipalities. The Tax Collector's property tax page lists each one with a phone number so you can ask the right office about its rate.

That list names the county, the Fire MSTU District, the Putnam County School Board, the St. Johns River Water Management District, the Suwannee Water Management District, and the City of Palatka, City of Crescent City, Town of Interlachen, Town of Pomona Park and Town of Welaka. A parcel inside a city pays that city's levy in addition to the county's.

Non-ad valorem charges sit beside the tax lines. The county enacted a solid waste special assessment for residential units, split between landfill improvements, garbage collection and recycling. The commissioners have also authorized 28 separate MSBU projects for road maintenance or paving, which charge only the properties that benefit. The Hastings Drainage District levies its own assessment. A buyer or seller can see these on the bill, and homestead exemption does not reduce them.

sections.h2: When are Putnam County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Taxes are assessed as of January 1 and bills usually open for collection on November 1. The gross amount is due by March 31, and unpaid real estate taxes become delinquent on April 1.

The collector also offers a quarterly installment plan for owners whose estimated bill is more than $100. The application must reach the office by April 30 of the year you want to begin. Payments fall due June 30 (6% discount), September 30 (4.5%), December 31 (3%) and March 31 (no discount). Missing the June payment removes the account from the plan, and under s. 197.222 the owner cannot rejoin until the next year with a new application. The first two payments use the prior year's taxes and the last two use the new roll.

sections.h2: What happens when Putnam County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquent parcels are advertised in a local newspaper once a week for three consecutive weeks, then a tax certificate sale is held online on or before June 1. The certificate is a lien and does not convey ownership.

Bidding starts at 18% and drops in quarter percent steps until the lowest bidder takes the certificate. After the sale, the Tax Collector's FAQ says the owner could pay interest up to 18% a year, depending on the bid rate. Delinquent taxes must be paid with cashier's check, certified check, cash or money order, and the date the office receives the payment sets the amount due.

  • In most cases, if taxes stay unpaid two years from April 1, the certificate holder can apply for a tax deed.
  • Applications go through RealTDA, and the county posts a Lands Available for Taxes list for parcels that did not sell.
  • Paying the taxes cancels the lien, but all payments after delinquency must be in certified funds.

Anyone selling a house with a certificate on it should ask the Tax Collector for a redemption figure and give it to the title company early, because interest keeps running.

sections.h2: What homestead and senior exemptions does the Putnam County appraiser offer?
sections.html:
The county appraiser's exemption page says the homestead exemption removes the first $25,000 of value from every ad valorem levy, and that it does not apply to special assessments. Applications are taken year-round at the Palatka office, with satellite filing from January 1 through March 1.

The deadline for all exemptions is March 1 following the year you buy. After that date you must also complete an Extenuating Circumstances form. The owner must hold title, be a Florida permanent resident and use the home as a primary residence on January 1. Proof of residency includes a Florida driver license or ID showing the home address and a Florida vehicle registration. Trust-owned homes face stricter review.

  • Low income senior exemption: a county ordinance adds $25,000 against the county general millage for owners 65 or older who meet the income limit; the office tells applicants to ask for the current limit.
  • Super Senior exemption: for 25-year residents with a just value under $250,000, which exempts the whole assessed value where a taxing authority has enacted it. The page names Putnam County, Palatka, Crescent City, Interlachen, Pomona Park and Welaka.
  • Deployed service member, total and permanent disability and first responder exemptions, each with their own proof requirements.

Once approved, an exemption renews automatically, but the owner must report changes in use or status right away under ss. 196.131 and 196.161.

sections.h2: How does a sale change the next Putnam County bill?
sections.html:
The next owner's bill is reset to just value in the following January, and any exemption you held does not follow the house. State rules treat a sale, foreclosure or transfer of title as a change of ownership, with exceptions for spouses and certain transfers at death.

That is why a bill for a house that has been in one family for years can look low next to what a new buyer sees on their first full roll. The Save Our Homes cap, which the Department of Revenue lists at 2.7% for 2026, applies only while the same owner keeps the homestead. If you are moving within Florida, the portability form can carry up to $500,000 of your accrued benefit to the new homestead, filed with the exemption application by March 1.

The deed also carries documentary stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 of consideration, collected by the Clerk when the deed records. All parties to the deed are liable even when the contract assigns payment to one side. Estate and probate transfers have separate treatment: the Department of Revenue says a personal representative's deed under a probated will is not taxable.

sections.h2: What should a Putnam County seller check before listing?
sections.html:
Confirm three things: that the current bill is paid or will be paid at closing, that no tax certificate has been issued, and that the exemption record matches how the house is used. Homestead ends if the unit is rented or stops being the permanent home.

The Tax Collector and the appraiser are both in Palatka, and the roll is public. Print the parcel record and the bill, and hand both to the closing agent. Putnam parcels can carry MSBU road assessments and a solid waste charge, so ask whether any are unpaid, since they ride on the same bill as the taxes.

faqs.q: What discount does Putnam County give for paying property tax early?
faqs.a: 4% in November, 3% in December, 2% in January and 1% in February, with no discount in March. Bills open for collection on November 1.

faqs.q: When does Putnam County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Taxes unpaid on March 31 are delinquent the next day and go to a tax certificate sale on or before June 1.

faqs.q: Is there a payment plan for Putnam County property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The quarterly installment plan needs an application by April 30 and an estimated bill above $100, with 6%, 4.5% and 3% discounts on the first three payments.

faqs.q: Where do I file for homestead in Putnam County?
faqs.a: File with the Property Appraiser in Palatka or at the Crescent City or Interlachen satellite offices from January 1 through March 1. The deadline is March 1 after you buy.

faqs.q: Can I lose my Putnam County house over unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, in the end. A certificate holder may apply for a tax deed after two years, and the house can then sell at auction, but you can redeem by paying the full amount before the deed sale.
